entries.non_ste_example: Utilize the Logger module to record error events.
entries.ste_example: Use the Logger module to record error events.
entries.explanation: P1 - "utilize" is not an approved word in the controlled terminology. Use "use" instead per the synonym table. The word "Logger" is a code-domain technical noun (category 6) and is allowed.

entries.non_ste_example: Install the frontend framework library before you build the user interface.
entries.ste_example: Install React before you build the user interface.
entries.explanation: P5 - "frontend framework library" is a descriptive phrase. Use the code-domain technical noun "React" (category 2: frameworks and runtimes) for the specific technology.

entries.non_ste_example: Perform an authentication operation on the client before you process the payment.
entries.ste_example: Authenticate the client before you process the payment.
entries.explanation: P12 - "perform an authentication operation" uses a general verb with a noun phrase. Use the code-domain technical verb "authenticate" (category 3: application operations) for the specific operation.

entries.non_ste_example: Send a query to the data query language endpoint to get the user profile.
entries.ste_example: Send a query to the GraphQL endpoint to get the user profile.
entries.explanation: P6 - "data query language endpoint" is a description instead of a technical noun. Use the code-domain technical noun "GraphQL" (category 19: network and protocol terms) for the specific technology. Non-approved words are allowed only as technical nouns.

entries.non_ste_example: Leverage the connection manager component to acquire a database handle for the migration.
entries.ste_example: Use the DatabasePool to get a connection for the migration.
entries.explanation: P1 - "leverage" is not an approved word (use "use" per the synonym table). P1 - "acquire" is not an approved word (use "get" per the synonym table). P5+P6 - "connection manager component" is a description; use the code-domain technical noun "DatabasePool" (category 6: modules, classes, and services).
